title: Arsenal Player Ratings vs. Borussia Dortmund: Gunners Endure Rare League Phase Blip
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack5:15 PM ESTArsenal rued missed chances. / Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesArsenal’s quest to secure a top-eight finish in the league phase table took a hit, as they were held to a 1–1 draw by Bundesliga leaders Borussia Dortmund at Emirates Stadium.

When Viktor Gyökeres thumped the hosts into an early lead, the majority would’ve expected Arsenal, who have yet to drop points at this stage of the competition under Mikel Arteta, to cruise to an all-too-familiar victory—the sort you’d forget in a hurry and perhaps be worthy of just a 90-second highlight reel.
Borussia Dortmund were miles off the pace, and although they gained a foothold toward the end of the first half, Arsenal ought to have been out of sight by halftime.

With their lead slender, as was the case after a dominant first half at Newcastle United on Saturday, Arsenal remained somewhat vulnerable, and Dortmund proved after the restart why they’re serious challengers for Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga throne.

A remarkable carry upfield from exciting young centerback Joane Gadou broke Arsenal’s press, and after Maximilian Beier beat Gabriel with a clever drift inside, Kepa Arrizabalaga was powerless to prevent the visitors equalizing.

Jobe Bellingham then thought he’d handed BVB an unlikely lead, which awoke the Gunners, who laid siege to Gregor Kobel’s goal until the match’s conclusion. And while gilt-edged chances came their way, the visitors held on for a well-earned point.

Gyökeres’ opening goal was emphatic. / Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesYou could argue that this was one of Viktor Gyökeres’ most encouraging performances in Arsenal red, despite the missed chances.

The opening goal was a sequence that supporters believed the Swede would produce on the regular when he arrived from Sporting CP two summers ago. Gyökeres took his shot from distance early to catch Gregor Köbel out, with the excellent Swiss goalkeeper undone by the dip.

It was emphatic from the brutish center forward, who also offered refinement against the Bundesliga leaders. His hold-up play and technical level has constantly come under scrutiny since joining the club, but it held up here. Gyökeres was able to combine comfortably off one touch and move freely within the frontline to create opportunities for him to run the channels.

Arteta understandably continues to trust Kai Havertz on the big occasion, but Gyökeres’s performance—if you overlook the profligacy post-goal—highlighted that he could play a bigger role for the Gunners when it matters most. He’s improving.

Needs a goal. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesArsenal supporters were wondering how they so easily prised Christos Tzolis away from Club Brugge in the summer, given the Greek’s sharp opening to his career in north London. Why wasn’t the rest of the continent keen?

Well, the initial enthusiasm has died down, perhaps not helped by a month-long absence due to injury. Formerly a clear upgrade on the serviceable and clutch Leandro Trossard, fans are suddenly desperate for the winger to merely replicate the Belgian’s level of performance.

Tzolis was certainly involved on Tuesday evening, and he’s clearly a smart attacker who can adhere to Arteta’s demands in possession. But the Greek star is currently struggling to piece it together in the final third, perhaps a little too desperate to score his first goal for the club.
Arsenal took an early lead.  / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*

GK: Kepa Arrizabalaga—7.3: You can hardly blame Kepa for a rare home concession in this competition. The reserve goalkeeper was otherwise kept relatively quiet, maintaining a composed demeanour throughout.

RB: Ben White—7.0: Always such a threat when he gets on the overlap, and his positioning inside freed up Noni Madueke on the touchline, contributing to the opening goal. Influence as an attacker reduced as the contest wore on.
CB: Ezri Konsa—7.0: A steady performance for Konsa, who entered this contest off the back of his toughest outing for the club at the weekend.
CB: Gabriel—7.3: Dortmund’s equalizer was crafted in a much deeper area, but Gabriel was beaten by Beier at the crucial moment.
LB: Piero Hincapié—7.9: Hincapié’s positioning was an issue for Dortmund throughout, whether that was in the half-space on down the flank.
